subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Wave behaviour and the wave equation

questions.q: Which is the correct wave equation relating wave speed (v), frequency (f) and wavelength (λ)?
questions.explain: Wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength (v = f λ).

questions.q: What is the unit of frequency?
questions.explain: Frequency is the number of waves per second, measured in hertz (Hz).

questions.q: In a transverse wave, the oscillations are...
options: perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer
parallel to the direction of energy transfer
in the same direction as energy transfer
always at 45 degrees to the direction of energy transfer
questions.explain: In a transverse wave the vibrations are at right angles to the direction the wave travels.

questions.q: Which of the following is a longitudinal wave?
questions.explain: Sound is longitudinal, with compressions and rarefactions along the direction of travel.

questions.q: The amplitude of a wave is...
options: the maximum displacement of a point from its rest position
the distance between two adjacent peaks
the number of waves per second
the time for one complete oscillation
questions.explain: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the undisturbed (rest) position.

questions.q: The wavelength of a wave is...
options: the distance from one point on a wave to the same point on the next wave
the height of a wave crest
the number of waves passing a point per second
questions.explain: Wavelength is the distance between two corresponding points on adjacent waves.

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 2 m. What is its speed?
questions.explain: Using v = f λ = 50 × 2 = 100 m/s.

questions.q: A wave has a period of 0.2 s. What is its frequency?
questions.explain: Frequency is the inverse of period: f = 1/T = 1/0.2 = 5 Hz.

questions.q: Which statement about electromagnetic waves is correct?
options: They are all transverse and travel at the same speed in a vacuum
They travel fastest as radio waves
They require a medium to travel through
questions.explain: All EM waves are transverse and travel at the speed of light in a vacuum.

questions.q: Which shows the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing frequency?
options: Radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma
Gamma, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwave, radio
Radio, infrared, microwave, visible, X-ray, ultraviolet, gamma
Visible, infrared, radio, microwave, gamma, X-ray, ultraviolet
questions.explain: Frequency increases from radio waves through to gamma rays.

questions.q: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum has the longest wavelength?
questions.explain: Radio waves have the longest wavelength and lowest frequency in the EM spectrum.

questions.q: Microwaves are suitable for heating food because they...
options: are absorbed by water molecules in the food
are reflected by all types of food
travel faster than other EM waves
have a high enough frequency to ionise atoms
questions.explain: Microwaves are absorbed by water molecules, transferring energy that heats the food.

questions.q: Why is over-exposure to ultraviolet radiation harmful to humans?
options: It can damage skin cells and increase the risk of skin cancer
It causes the skin to freeze
It has no effect on the human body
It weakens bones by removing calcium
questions.explain: UV can damage cells and cause premature ageing and skin cancer.

questions.q: Gamma rays can be used to sterilise surgical instruments because they...
options: coat the instruments in a protective layer
questions.explain: Gamma rays are ionising and kill bacteria, sterilising the equipment.

questions.q: An alpha particle consists of...
questions.explain: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus, made of 2 protons and 2 neutrons.

questions.q: A beta particle can be stopped by...
questions.explain: Beta radiation is blocked by a few millimetres of aluminium; paper stops only alpha.

questions.q: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is...
options: the time taken for half the undecayed nuclei to decay
the time taken for all the nuclei to decay
the number of decays per second
half the total mass of the sample
questions.explain: Half-life is the time for half the remaining unstable nuclei (or the count rate) to halve.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes nuclear fusion?
options: Two light nuclei join together to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy
A large nucleus splits into two smaller nuclei
A neutron is absorbed and the nucleus becomes stable
An electron is emitted from the nucleus
questions.explain: Fusion joins two light nuclei into a heavier one, releasing energy, as in the Sun.

questions.q: A sample has a count rate of 800 counts/min and a half-life of 2 hours. What will the count rate be after 6 hours?
questions.explain: 6 hours is 3 half-lives: 800 to 400 to 200 to 100 counts/min.

questions.q: A nucleus with mass number 226 and atomic number 88 emits an alpha particle. What are the mass and atomic numbers of the new nucleus?
questions.explain: Alpha decay reduces the mass number by 4 and the atomic number by 2.
